title: Why Earth Has a Magnetic Shield

post_description: Where Earth's magnetic field comes from and what it does, from NASA and USGS. Sources: National Aeronautics and Space Administration https://science.nasa.gov/science-research/earth-science/earths-magnetosphere-protecting-our-planet-from-harmful-space-energy/ and United States Geological Survey https://www.usgs.gov/programs/geomagnetism/introduction-geomagnetism #Science #ScienceFacts #QuantaTale
narration: What invisible shield protects Earth from the solar wind? Almost all of Earth's magnetic field starts in its fluid outer core. Churning molten metal there generates electrical currents hundreds of miles wide. Scientists call this mechanism the geodynamo. The field has two poles, like a bar magnet. Unlike Mercury, Venus and Mars, Earth wears a huge magnetic field called the magnetosphere. It shields us from solar wind that would erode the atmosphere. Over time the poles drift, and every now and then they flip completely.
